cards.name: Show Grid
cards.summary: Toggles the perspective grid on the canvas: shows the active perspective grid (the default two-point grid if none has been set) so art can be drawn or attached onto its left, right and floor planes; the label switches to Hide Grid while it is visible.
use_for: drawing packaging, storefront or building illustrations in correct two- or three-point perspective
placing signage, logos or text onto the side of a box or wall mock-up
laying out street, shop or room scenes in perspective for infographics or editorial illustration
avoid: flat layouts that need no perspective: the grid's widget and planes get in the way, hide it again with the same shortcut
curved surfaces such as bottles, cans or bags: the grid has only flat planes, use Object > Mockup or Effect > 3D and Materials instead
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("Show Perspective Grid") (id paired by its default shortcut, not confirmed by execution). DOM: app.activeDocument.showPerspectiveGrid() / hidePerspectiveGrid() (harvested methods).

review.changes: use_for: 'isometric-looking scenes' dropped (the grid has vanishing points, isometric has none); avoid: Photoshop's Vanishing Point is flat-plane too, so it is no answer for curved surfaces, now Object > Mockup or Effect > 3D and Materials

cards.name: Show Rulers
cards.summary: Toggles a measuring ruler on the perspective grid itself (drawn along the grid's true height line, in the grid's units), separate from the document rulers; it only shows while the perspective grid is visible.
use_for: sizing a door, window or shelf to a real height while drawing a storefront or interior in perspective
keeping repeated objects (posts, bottles, signs) the same height across a perspective scene
avoid: measuring the document or artboard: use View > Rulers > Show Rulers, this ruler belongs only to the perspective grid
expecting it to show with the grid hidden: show the grid first (Shift+Ctrl+I)

review.changes: avoid: removed the shortcut Ctrl+R (another item's shortcut, not in this batch)

cards.name: Snap to Grid
cards.summary: Toggles snapping to the perspective grid: while on, objects drawn, moved or attached with the perspective tools snap to the grid lines of the active plane. It is separate from View > Snap to Grid, which snaps to the flat document grid.
use_for: lining up windows, panels or shelves exactly on grid cells in an architectural or packaging illustration
keeping repeated perspective elements (tiles, fence posts) evenly spaced
avoid: free placement between grid lines feels sticky: turn it off temporarily, or set a finer grid cell size in View > Perspective Grid > Define Grid
snapping flat (non-perspective) art: use View > Snap to Grid or Smart Guides instead
cards.script_api: No executeMenuCommand id was paired in the harvest; the harvest's fallback is the menu path or Win32 command 2147484348. DOM substitute: none known; Document.isSnapToGridEnabled() in the harvest reads the document grid snap, not this one (unverified).

cards.name: [3P-Normal View]
cards.summary: Switches the document's perspective grid to Illustrator's built-in three-point preset: left and right vanishing points on the horizon plus a third vertical vanishing point, so vertical lines also converge (a tall building seen from above or below).
use_for: dramatic skyscraper or tower illustrations where verticals must converge
city scenes seen from street level or from the air where building verticals must lean together
a starting grid to tweak with the Perspective Grid tool before saving a custom preset
avoid: ordinary product or room views: the converging verticals look distorted, use [2P-Normal View]
art already attached to a different grid: changing the preset does not re-project existing perspective objects, check them after switching

cards.name: [2P-Normal View]

use_for: box and packaging mock-ups seen corner-on
street corners, shopfronts and room interiors for editorial or explainer illustrations
resetting a grid that has been dragged out of shape back to a clean starting point
avoid: looking straight at a wall or down a corridor: use the one-point preset ([1P-Normal View])
very tall subjects whose verticals should converge: use [3P-Normal View]

cards.name: Pixel Preview
cards.summary: Toggles Pixel Preview: the document is drawn as it will look when rasterised at screen resolution, showing anti-aliasing and blurry half-pixel edges; the artwork stays vector.
use_for: checking icons, UI elements and web graphics for crisp pixel-aligned edges before export
previewing thin strokes and small type as they will render in PNG or GIF exports
spotting soft edges on banner ads and social graphics
avoid: print work: it shows screen pixels, not print output, use Overprint Preview or a PDF proof instead
fixing edges by eye only: also use Snap to Pixel / Align to Pixel Grid so edges actually land on whole pixels
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("raster") (id paired by its default shortcut, not confirmed by execution). DOM: app.activeDocument.getPreviewMode() reads the mode; DocumentPreset.previewMode = DocumentPreviewMode.PixelPreview sets it only for a new document (harvested).

cards.name: Presentation Mode
cards.summary: Shows the active artboard full screen on a black background with menus, panels and guides hidden, like a slide show; the other artboards are stepped through from the keyboard, and the normal view returns when you leave the mode.
use_for: presenting logo options or a multi-artboard pitch to a client straight from the .ai file
a clean, distraction-free check of each social or poster artboard at full screen
walking through a storyboard laid out one frame per artboard
avoid: editing: tools do not work in this mode, leave it first to make changes
sending to someone without Illustrator: export a PDF of the artboards instead

cards.name: Preview
cards.summary: The Ctrl+Y view toggle between Outline mode (paths only, no fills or strokes) and Preview mode (full colour artwork); the harvested label is Preview, the state that the toggle leads to from Outline mode. It changes only the display.
use_for: returning to full-colour view after checking paths in Outline mode
flipping to outlines to find hidden, stacked or stray paths, then back to judge the finished look
speeding up work on very heavy files by drawing in outline and previewing only when needed
avoid: outlining or previewing one layer only: untick Preview in that layer's Layer Options (Layers panel) instead of switching the whole document
checking overprint or rasterised output: use Overprint Preview or Pixel Preview

cards.name: Proof Colors
cards.summary: Toggles soft proofing: the screen simulates how the colours will reproduce on the output chosen in View > Proof Setup (document CMYK, an RGB display or a colour-blindness simulation); a tick shows it is on and the file's colours are not changed.
use_for: checking that bright RGB brand colours survive conversion before sending a CMYK print job
previewing a design under a colour-blindness simulation for accessibility
comparing how a web graphic looks on an unmanaged display
avoid: final colour approval on an uncalibrated monitor: soft proofs are only as good as the monitor profile, ask for a hard proof
leaving it on while picking colours for screen output: it skews what you see, turn it off afterwards
cards.script_api: app.executeMenuCommand("proofColors") (id paired by its words matching the menu label, not confirmed by execution). It toggles, and no harvested DOM call reads whether proofing is on.

cards.name: Color blindness - Deuteranopia-type
cards.summary: Sets the soft-proof condition to simulate green-weak (deuteranopia-type) colour vision, the most common form, where reds and greens of similar lightness are hard to tell apart. The simulation shows on screen while View > Proof Colors is ticked; the artwork is not changed.
use_for: checking that charts, maps and infographics do not rely on a red/green colour difference
testing traffic-light status colours in a UI or dashboard for readability
avoid: treating it as proof of full accessibility: it does not cover tritanopia or low vision, also check contrast ratios
forgetting to switch the proof back: reset View > Proof Setup to Document CMYK before judging print colour

cards.name: Color blindness - Protanopia-type
cards.summary: Sets the soft-proof condition to simulate red-weak (protanopia-type) colour vision, where reds look darker and duller and red/green pairs merge. The simulation shows on screen while View > Proof Colors is ticked; the artwork is not changed.
use_for: checking that red warning text, sale badges or error states still stand out against dark or green backgrounds
testing a brand palette's red accent for legibility for red-weak viewers
avoid: treating it as proof of full accessibility: it does not cover tritanopia or low vision, also check contrast ratios
forgetting to switch the proof back: reset View > Proof Setup to Document CMYK before judging print colour

cards.name: Customize...
cards.summary: Opens the Customize Proof Condition dialog, where any ICC profile can be chosen as the device to simulate for soft proofing (a specific press, paper or display profile), instead of the fixed presets in the Proof Setup menu.
cards.how: Choose the Device to Simulate (the printer's or paper's ICC profile), decide whether to Preserve Numbers (simulate sending the numbers unconverted) and pick a rendering intent; under Display Options tick Simulate Paper Color for a realistic, duller paper white. Then turn on View > Proof Colors. (Field names from Illustrator's documentation; the harvest has no params for this dialog.)
use_for: soft-proofing a job against the printer's supplied ICC profile, e.g. uncoated or newsprint stock
previewing how packaging colours shift on a specific press condition before a hard proof
avoid: no profile from the printer: guessing a profile gives false confidence, ask for one or use Document CMYK
expecting it to convert the file: it only changes the on-screen simulation, use the colour conversion in the PDF export settings (or File > Document Color Mode) for that
